requirements.requirement: HTTP methods, headers, bodies and complete status results
requirements.details: Text is strict UTF-8; binary bodies and header values preserve bytes. Duplicate values and trailers are bounded. 4xx/5xx are normal complete responses; partial responses are errors.

requirements.requirement: Verified HTTPS and explicit redirect/retry policy
requirements.details: Redirects/retries default off. Cross-origin requests drop all user headers and require an empty GET/HEAD; HTTPS downgrade fails. Retryable statuses are explicit, transport errors are not retried, and fixed delays/counts share one deadline.

requirements.requirement: Cancellation, ownership, deadlines and evaluator compatibility
requirements.details: Connections are polled inside the owned request future. Started platform DNS workers retain leases until completion. Stops bypass Catch and Finally has independent cleanup. HTTP futures are boxed to preserve recursive evaluator stack bounds; CLI enables I/O.

requirements.requirement: Bounded input, output, temporary overlap and global capacity
requirements.details: 32 slots and 64 MiB logical shared bytes; 4 MiB workspace plus maximum output are admitted before network effects. Parser, URL, input, headers and streamed body have independent caps. Run value and temporary quotas apply.

97 fixed signatures, example 34, HTTP reference and B7 corpus. 1695 tests per GNU/musl debug/release profile; strict lint and format checks, 100 full HTTP repetitions (2200 passes), all 19 focused faults caught.

limitations: HTTP/1.1 only, no proxies, automatic decompression, cookie jar, client certificates or streaming response API.
Retry-After is not interpreted; only explicitly documented safe-method status retries use the configured fixed delay.
The host network is not sandboxed. Started OS DNS cannot be forcibly stopped and can delay Tokio runtime shutdown; admission remains retained.
Budgets measure logical owned payload and bounded buffers, not allocator, kernel or resolver RSS.
